transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah. Nice to meet you. 

...I guess my supervisor at work is the one who wanted me to come. I, uh... I said something to him the other day. I've just been having these thoughts lately. Stuff like... maybe my family would be better off if I just didn't wake up. 

It, um... it spooked me a little bit, having a thought like that. So I mentioned it to him, and... well, now I'm here. That's about it.
Are you thinking about killing yourself right now?
No... no, I'm not. Just... like I said, it was just a thought that crossed my mind. I wouldn't actually do anything.
Have you been feeling depressed lately?
I don't know if I'd use that word. Just... maybe a little down, I guess. I don't really think about it too much.
Did something stressful happen recently before these thoughts started?

I don't know about stressful. Just... things change, I guess. My daughter, she... she left Georgia for the military. That was about two weeks ago. I suppose I've felt a little different since then. But it's not a big deal.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

I suppose. I mean... I used to mess with my tomato plants out back, maybe sand some wood at my bench. Watch the Falcons on Sunday, stay after church to talk with folks... but lately, I don't know. I just look at all that and it feels like... like it belongs to somebody else. I just haven't had the energy for it.
For most of the day lately, have you been feeling sad or down?
I wouldn't say sad. Just... I don't know. I'm mostly just keeping to myself right now. I don't really pay attention to the clock to see how long it lasts.
Have these changes been making it hard for you to do your usual work or take care of things at home?

I guess so. At work... well, I messed up a few things. It got to the point where my supervisor found me just sitting in my truck before my shift. Real early in the morning. He ended up getting occupational health involved. And at the house... I don't know. I just haven't been opening the mail. The bills are just sitting there. I usually take care of all that, but... I just haven't.
Have these changes been going on nearly every day for at least two weeks?
Yeah, I reckon so. It's been... right at about two weeks. Ever since my daughter left Georgia. She went into the military. So, yeah. Just been like this since then.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

I suppose so. At the distribution center... I'll just be staring at the schedule, or the routing sheet, and my mind just won't lock in. Even little staffing calls feel... bigger than they ought to. Just can't seem to focus on it.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?
I don't know... sleep's been alright, I guess. Haven't really noticed a problem.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite lately?

Yeah, I guess so. I just... I don't really have much of one right now. Most days I kind of have to force myself to just take a few bites. Even stuff I usually like... whether I'm at the warehouse or at home, it just kind of sits there. End up throwing most of it out, to be honest.
Have you been moving or talking more slowly than usual lately?

I guess maybe a little. The guys at work keep asking if I'm coming down with something. Say I'm... walking slower, taking a while to just answer them when they ask about the shift. I don't know, it just... feels like I'm moving through mud sometimes.
Lately, have you been feeling worthless or like you're a burden to your family?

I don't know about worthless. Just... been thinking a lot, I guess. 

My daughter leaving, I just... I keep going over it in my head. It's hard not to think I must have failed her somehow. Like maybe... I don't know. Like a better father would have done something different. Just been on my mind, that's all.
Before these past two weeks, have you ever had another period like this in your life?

I guess... yeah. There's been other times. 

For about a year now, I've had these... low stretches, I suppose you could call them. They come and go. But this one... since she left... it's just been heavier. Hit me a lot harder than the others.
Before this current period, was there ever a time when these low stretches lasted at least two weeks?
I'm not really sure. I don't keep track of the days like that. They just... happen. I don't know if it was two weeks.
In those earlier low stretches, did any one of them last two weeks or longer?
I already told you... I don't know. I don't mark it on a calendar. It's just... a while. I don't know if it was two weeks.
During those earlier low stretches, did you also lose interest in the things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I guess. I used to... I don't know, mess with my tomato plants out back. Sand wood at my workbench. Even watching the Falcons or staying after church to talk with folks. Just... lately, I look at all that and it feels like it belongs to somebody else. I just don't care about it.
During those earlier low stretches, did they ever make it hard for you to function at work or at home?

Yeah, I suppose so. At work... well, I made some mistakes. Bad enough that one morning a supervisor found me just sitting out in my truck before the sun even came up. They ended up getting occupational health involved after that. And at home... I don't know, I just let things go. Bills pile up on the counter. Things I usually take care of, I just... leave them sitting there.
Before this current spell, was there ever a time when these symptoms stayed bad for at least two weeks in a row?

Like I said, I don't know about back then. I didn't keep track. But... this whole change in me right now, it's been going on for about two weeks. Just... ever since my daughter left Georgia for the military. That's all I can tell you.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually up or energetic compared with your normal self?

I guess so. There was a stretch where I... well, I just had a whole lot of energy. I'd be up way before daylight, figuring out plans to change the warehouse around. Then I'd be out cleaning the garage. Just... jumping from one job to the next. I didn't really want to stop.
